paper_title: Context Consistency between Training and Testing in Simultaneous Machine   Translation
caption: Comparison of correlation between training loss (cross-entropy objective loss for Consistency-CE and Bi-objective loss for Consistency-Bi) and translation quality (BLEU score) on train subset of WMT15 De-En task for wait-k policy.
model_annotation: The line plot compares the correlation between training loss and translation quality (measured by BLEU score) for two models—Consistency-CE and Consistency-Bi—on the train subset of the WMT15 De-En task under a wait-k policy. The x-axis represents the testing parameter $k$, ranging from 2 to 9 in integer steps, while the y-axis shows the correlation value, scaled from 0.5 to 0.9. The Consistency-CE model, represented by a blue dashed line with circular markers, begins at a correlation of approximately 0.62 when $k=2$, increases steadily to about 0.75 at $k=9$. In contrast, the Consistency-Bi model, shown as an orange solid line with square markers, starts at a higher correlation of around 0.92 at $k=2$ and remains relatively stable, slightly increasing to approximately 0.95 at $k=9$. Both models show positive trends, but Consistency-Bi maintains consistently higher correlation values across all tested $k$ values.
